title: Decision Mode Governance Rules
description: JSON Schema for governance rules applied to macp.mode.decision.v1 sessions. See RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1.

algorithm.description: Voting algorithm. 'none' means no voting constraint is enforced.

threshold.description: Fraction of the decisive votes required for approval. Used by the 'majority', 'supermajority', and 'weighted' algorithms. Must be greater than 0; at least 0.5 for 'majority'; greater than 0.5 for 'supermajority'. Abstentions are excluded from the denominator, and under 'weighted' so are weight-0 votes. See RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1.
threshold.$comment: exclusiveMinimum 0: threshold 0 made an all-REJECT round return Passed under both majority and weighted (issue #98, item 2).

quorum.description: Minimum participation bar. Applied only when commitment.require_vote_quorum is true; on its own this object gates nothing. See RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1.

value.description: Minimum number of participants that must vote ('count'), or the minimum share of declared participants that must vote as a percentage in 0-100 ('percentage').

weights.description: Per-participant vote weights; keys are participant IDs. Used only with the 'weighted' algorithm. This map is the weighted electorate: a declared participant absent from it has weight 0 (observers are expressed by omission), and a weight-0 vote is NON-DECISIVE — it contributes to neither side of the ratio, does not enter the decisive tally, and does not satisfy the decline guard of RFC-MACP-0007 Section 6.2, though it still counts as a vote cast for the voting.quorum participation floor. Values must be greater than 0 and the map must be non-empty. Those two constraints are enforced UNCONDITIONALLY, at every algorithm, not only under 'weighted': a weights map is meaningless elsewhere, so an empty or zero-valued one is a policy-authoring error wherever it appears. This electorate rule is normative for EVERY schema version, not only 3. See RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1.
weights.$comment: exclusiveMinimum 0 + minProperties 1: an all-zero or empty weights map yielded 'no votes' on a COMPLETE ballot set (issue #98, item 3). A legitimately zero-weighted observer is expressed by omission from this map, not by an explicit 0, so nothing is lost.

objection_handling.description: How blocking objections affect commitment eligibility.

critical_severity_vetoes.description: If true, objections with severity 'critical' prevent commitment.

veto_threshold.description: Number of blocking objections required to veto commitment.

critical_objection_action.description: Action when a critical objection would block commitment: deny (reject the commitment), finalize_decline (resolve the session as a negative outcome), or hold (reject the commitment as deny does, annotated as an escalation). deny and hold are observationally identical — both reject with POLICY_DENIED and leave the session OPEN; hold is an operator-facing annotation, not a distinct protocol outcome. See RFC-MACP-0012 §4.1.

evaluation.description: Constraints on evaluations before voting or commitment.

minimum_confidence.description: Minimum confidence level for evaluations to be considered valid.

required_before_voting.description: If true, at least one evaluation must exist before votes are counted.

commitment.description: Who can commit and under what conditions.

authority.description: Who is authorized to emit a Commitment.

designated_roles.description: Participant IDs or roles authorized to commit. Used only with 'designated_role' authority.

require_vote_quorum.description: If true, commitment is only allowed after vote quorum is met.

allow_decline_over_approval.description: If true, a negative commitment (outcome_positive=false) is allowed even when the vote passed.

allOf.$comment: 'supermajority' REQUIRES threshold, deliberately asymmetric with the majority arm below, which constrains the value without requiring the key. Without 'required' this arm was self-contradicting: {"algorithm": "supermajority"} validated, and the threshold subschema's own default of 0.5 then supplied a value this very arm declares illegal -- a supermajority that is a bare majority wearing the name (issue #101). Safe to require: all five supermajority rule blocks on disk set threshold explicitly.

'majority' means at least half: inclusive minimum 0.5, deliberately asymmetric with the supermajority arm's exclusiveMinimum. RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1 pins the comparison as inclusive so an even split approves, and the reserved policy.std.majority profile sets threshold exactly 0.5 — exclusiveMinimum here would invalidate a profile Section 2.2 pins byte-identical on every runtime. Constrains the value only; adding 'required' would reject the four existing majority rule blocks that omit threshold entirely.
